findings.title: google_notebooks_runtime.main never wires var.network/var.subnet, so it lands on the project's default VPC
findings.explanation: The module declares var.network and var.subnet as inputs and google_notebooks_instance.main correctly consumes them (network = var.network, subnet = var.subnet in google_notebooks_instance.main.tf:16-17). google_notebooks_runtime.main.tf's virtual_machine_config block never sets network/subnet even though the provider schema exposes both attributes there — so at apply time GCP attaches the runtime's VM to the project's default auto-mode VPC instead of the caller-supplied private network. Per-resource deterministic checks (HLD_GCP_235: internal_ip_only) still pass because they only look at whether the VM has an external IP, not which network it lands on, so this composition gap is invisible to a single-resource rule. The variable's own description text ('ID of the private VPC network for the legacy notebooks instance', variables.tf:47) hints this was scoped to the legacy resource only and never extended — whether that's intentional or an oversight, it means two of the module's three notebook resources silently bypass the network isolation the module's own interface advertises to callers.
findings.remediation: Add network = var.network and subnet = var.subnet inside google_notebooks_runtime.main's virtual_machine_config block, matching the pattern already used by google_notebooks_instance.main.
findings.fix:
Insert after the `internal_ip_only = true` line inside virtual_machine_config:

      network = var.network
      subnet  = var.subnet

findings.title: google_workbench_instance.main never wires var.network/var.subnet, so it lands on the project's default VPC
findings.explanation: Same gap as HOLDEN_AI_001, on the third notebook resource. google_workbench_instance.main.tf's gce_setup block never sets a network_interfaces block, even though the provider schema exposes network_interfaces { network, subnet } there for exactly this purpose. gce_setup.disable_public_ip = true (satisfying HLD_GCP_231) only guarantees no external IP — it says nothing about which VPC the instance's internal interface lands on. Without an explicit network_interfaces block, GCP attaches the instance to the project's default auto-mode VPC network instead of the private network the caller passed in via var.network/var.subnet, which the sibling google_notebooks_instance.main does honor.
findings.remediation: Add a network_interfaces { network = var.network, subnet = var.subnet } block inside google_workbench_instance.main's gce_setup block.

findings.title: google_notebooks_instance.main omits service_account, defaulting to the project's Compute Engine default service account
findings.explanation: google_notebooks_instance exposes a top-level service_account attribute whose provider documentation states plainly: 'If not specified, the Compute Engine default service account is used.' That default account has historically carried the broad Editor role in many projects, and even where it doesn't, it's an ambient identity shared with every other unscoped workload in the project rather than one scoped to this notebook. Holden already enforces this exact 'no default Compute Engine SA' pattern for 10+ other GCP resource families (HLD_GCP_038 for GCE instances, HLD_GCP_084 for Cloud Run, HLD_GCP_179 for Cloud Functions, etc.) but has no equivalent check for google_notebooks_instance — a genuine coverage gap, not a false alarm, since the pattern and its rationale are already established holden precedent for every other GCE-backed compute resource type.
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated google_service_account scoped to only the roles the notebook workload needs (e.g. object access to the specific GCS buckets/BigQuery datasets it reads), and set service_account = google_service_account.notebooks.email on google_notebooks_instance.main. The right role set depends on what the notebook actually does, so this isn't a mechanical fix.

findings.title: google_workbench_instance.main omits gce_setup.service_accounts, defaulting to the project's Compute Engine default service account
findings.explanation: Same pattern as HOLDEN_AI_003: gce_setup.service_accounts[].email is left unset, so GCP attaches the project's Compute Engine default service account to the Workbench VM. Any code executed through the JupyterLab interface — which is precisely what a Workbench instance exists to run — inherits that ambient identity's access. This mirrors an established holden pattern (HLD_GCP_038, HLD_GCP_084, HLD_GCP_179, etc.) not yet extended to google_workbench_instance.
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated google_service_account and set gce_setup.service_accounts { email = google_service_account.notebooks.email } on google_workbench_instance.main. The right role set depends on the workload, so this isn't a mechanical fix.

suggested_policies.rationale: Holden already enforces 'no default Compute Engine service account' across 10+ GCP compute-adjacent resource families (google_compute_instance, google_cloud_run_service, google_cloudfunctions_function, google_composer_environment, etc.) but has no equivalent for google_notebooks_instance, despite it exposing the identical service_account attribute with the identical unsafe default per its own provider documentation. This closes that gap using the same all:/not_null/not_matches pattern already used by HLD_GCP_038.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Vertex AI Notebooks instances must not use the default Compute Engine service account
principle: identity-and-access
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  If google_notebooks_instance.service_account is left unset, GCP attaches the
  project's Compute Engine default service account, which historically carries
  the broad `Editor` role. Any code executed on the notebook (including
  arbitrary user-supplied notebook cells) inherits that identity's full
  project-wide access, turning a single compromised or malicious notebook
  session into a path to broad project compromise.
remediation: |
  Create a dedicated service account scoped to only the roles the notebook
  workload needs, and reference it explicitly:

  resource "google_notebooks_instance" "main" {
    service_account = google_service_account.notebooks.email
  }
resources:
  google_notebooks_instance:
    all:
      - path: service_account
        not_null: true
      - path: service_account
        not_matches: ".*-compute@developer\\.gserviceaccount\\.com$"

suggested_policies.rationale: Same gap as above, on google_workbench_instance's gce_setup.service_accounts. Not currently covered by any policy in coverage_by_type for google_workbench_instance (only HLD_GCP_230/CMEK and HLD_GCP_231/public-IP exist).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Vertex AI Workbench instances must not use the default Compute Engine service account
principle: identity-and-access
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  If gce_setup.service_accounts is left unset, GCP attaches the project's
  Compute Engine default service account to the Workbench instance's
  underlying VM. Any code executed through the JupyterLab interface inherits
  that identity's full project-wide access, turning a single compromised or
  malicious notebook session into a path to broad project compromise.
remediation: |
  Create a dedicated service account scoped to only the roles the workload
  needs, and reference it explicitly:

  resource "google_workbench_instance" "main" {
    gce_setup {
      service_accounts {
        email = google_service_account.notebooks.email
      }
    }
  }
resources:
  google_workbench_instance:
    all:
      - path: gce_setup.service_accounts.email
        not_null: true
      - path: gce_setup.service_accounts.email
        not_matches: ".*-compute@developer\\.gserviceaccount\\.com$"

suggested_policies.rationale: Generic, module-independent version of HOLDEN_AI_001: any google_notebooks_runtime with no explicit network lands on the project's default auto-mode VPC, which carries permissive implicit firewall rules unless the project has removed them. Not covered by any existing policy for this resource type (only HLD_GCP_234/CMEK and HLD_GCP_235/external-IP exist).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_003
name: Vertex AI Notebooks runtimes must specify an explicit VPC network
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  If virtual_machine_config.network is left unset, GCP attaches the runtime's
  VM to the project's default auto-mode VPC network instead of a
  purpose-built private network. The default network ships with permissive
  implicit firewall rules (SSH/RDP/ICMP open from 0.0.0.0/0 unless the
  project has explicitly removed them), so a runtime placed there inherits a
  broader attack surface than one deliberately placed on a hardened,
  isolated network.
remediation: |
  resource "google_notebooks_runtime" "main" {
    virtual_machine {
      virtual_machine_config {
        network = google_compute_network.private.id
        subnet  = google_compute_subnetwork.private.id
      }
    }
  }
resources:
  google_notebooks_runtime:
    path: virtual_machine.virtual_machine_config.network
    not_null: true

suggested_policies.rationale: Generic, module-independent version of HOLDEN_AI_002, mirroring HLD_PROPOSED_003 for google_workbench_instance's gce_setup.network_interfaces. Not covered by any existing policy for this resource type.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_004
name: Vertex AI Workbench instances must specify an explicit VPC network
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  If gce_setup.network_interfaces is left unset, GCP attaches the Workbench
  instance's VM to the project's default auto-mode VPC network instead of a
  purpose-built private network. The default network ships with permissive
  implicit firewall rules (SSH/RDP/ICMP open from 0.0.0.0/0 unless the
  project has explicitly removed them), so an instance placed there inherits
  a broader attack surface than one deliberately placed on a hardened,
  isolated network.
remediation: |
  resource "google_workbench_instance" "main" {
    gce_setup {
      network_interfaces {
        network = google_compute_network.private.id
        subnet  = google_compute_subnetwork.private.id
      }
    }
  }
resources:
  google_workbench_instance:
    path: gce_setup.network_interfaces.network
    not_null: true
